The exploration of noninvasive continuous glucose monitoring, as meticulously documented in John L. Smith’s “The Pursuit of Noninvasive Glucose: ‘Hunting the Deceitful Turkey’,” is a remarkable narrative that spans over 35 years. Smith’s dedication to advancing noninvasive glucose measurement technologies is evident throughout his work, even though the journey has been marked by numerous challenges and technological dead ends.
In his pursuit, Smith has witnessed and critically evaluated a wide array of technological developments and proposals. He has seen everything from near-infrared and mid-infrared techniques to photoacoustic, PPG, Raman, and even saliva, sweat, and tears-based methods. His expertise allows him to sift through the noise, highlighting only the most innovative, noteworthy, or promising developments.
One of the more recent trends in this field is the exploration of pulse wave data (PPG) for noninvasive blood glucose and pressure information. Although results have so far been inconclusive, the continued efforts in this area demonstrate the relentless pursuit of a viable solution.
